text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Croat member of Bosnian collective presidency Kresimir Zubak asks head of World Bank mission, Rory O'Sullivan, to determine whether bank loans approved for Bosnian budget were used for that purpose. He says Bosnian Government has not yet decided how to spend $30 million of $90 million in loans from World Bank.

- Ruling Moslem Party of Democratic Action (SDA) supports set of election rules designed by Provisional Election Commission (PEC) of Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE). SDA thinks this is step towards reducing possibility of voting at new address, head of SDA General Board Halid Genjac tells news conference.

- Bosnian Council of Ministers reaches agreement on draft for working relations and concludes that commissions charged with drafting laws on economic policy should complete their work within seven days.

- Working groups of Bosnian Council of Ministers will meet every day and it is hoped they will finish job by middle of next week, says international High Representative for Bosnia, Carl Bildt, after Council meeting. He says Brussels donors conference will not be held until package of economic laws is adopted.

- Joint List coalition of five Bosnian opposition parties will participate in upcoming local elections but not in countrywide parliamentary elections scheduled for 1998, senior member Stjepan Kljuic says. He denies rumours of Joint List's disintegration.

- "We cannot accept that everybody has to pay a price because some people are constantly obstructing the implementation of the Dayton agreement," Moslem-Croat Federation Prime Minister Edhem Bicakcic says in Strasbourg at session of Council of Europe.

- Officials of Bosnian Council of Ministers agree to establish telephone lines between each other and to that end they ask for assistance of Office of the international High Representative. Normal telephone lines between Bosnian Serb Republic and Moslem-Croat Federation not yet established.

- Team of experts from Moslem-Croat Federation's Health Ministry confirms flu epidemic in Federation, citing huge number of sick people. It says number of sick could exceed 100,000 within the next four weeks.

- Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic will instruct local authorities on procedures related to separation zones between Bosnian Serb Republic and Bosnia's Moslem-Croat Federation, officials from Office of the international High Representative for Bosnia say.
